title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Sutter Health in 2026
summary: Requesting Sutter Health records? Get the SH-0009 form walkthrough, central fax and mailing details, California deadlines and fees, plus how Codes Health helps law firms.
body_markdown:
Requesting medical records from Sutter Health takes specific forms, correct contact information, and attention to California's legal timelines. Sutter handles most requests through a centralized Release of Information (ROI) process covering its hospitals and care locations across Northern California. Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing required information can delay processing, so correct deficiencies promptly and document when Sutter received a valid request; don't assume every correction automatically restarts the[applicable deadline](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=123110) . For personal injury law firms handling multiple Sutter Health cases,[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) supports record retrieval through request checking, provider coordination, and status tracking, typically returning organized records in a couple of weeks.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Sutter Health requires a completed Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Health Information form (Form SH-0009), identification, and supporting authority documentation for most representative requests


-


The central ROI fax is 916-736-5499 and the mailing address is PO Box 619091, Roseville, CA 95661, though some facilities have dedicated Health Information Management departments


-


Sutter asks requesters to allow up to[15 calendar days](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=123110) after it receives a written request


-


For qualifying pre-litigation requests under[Evidence Code § 1158](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EVID&sectionNum=1158) , records must be made available for inspection and copying within 5 days after presentation of the written authorization


-


Sutter's form includes five protected-information selections; select only the categories the patient authorizes and leave them blank when none applies


-


Codes Health checks authorizations before submission to help reduce preventable rejections from missing signatures, unchecked boxes, and incomplete fields


## **Understanding Sutter Health Medical Record Request Forms: Your Guide to a HIPAA Release**


### **What is a HIPAA Release Form and Why Do You Need It?**


A HIPAA release form authorizes a provider to disclose protected health information (PHI) to a designated third party. Covered entities like Sutter can't release records without[written patient authorization](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/privacy/hipaa-privacy) unless a specific exception applies.


Sutter's form includes separate permissions for specified protected information. Additional requirements depend on the record type and applicable state and federal law.


### **Key Sections of a Sutter Health Medical Records Request Form**


Sutter Health's primary authorization form, "Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Health Information" (Form SH-0009), contains several key sections:


**Patient Identification:**


-


Complete legal name matching medical records exactly


-


Date of birth in MM/DD/YYYY format


-


Current address, phone number, and email


-


Medical record number if available


**Facility and Provider Information:**


-


Specific Sutter Health facility where care was received


-


Date range of treatment requested


-


Types of records needed (clinic notes, hospital records, lab results, imaging reports)


**Recipient Information:**


-


Law firm name and complete mailing address


-


Phone and fax numbers for delivery coordination


-


Preferred delivery method (encrypted or unencrypted email, encrypted CD or USB, paper, portal, or fax with a 50-page limit)


**Sensitive Information Authorization:**


-


[Separate selections required](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records) for protected categories such as HIV test results, mental health records, substance use treatment, genetic testing, and abortion-related records, with instructions addressing out-of-state disclosure


-


Select only the categories the patient authorizes, and leave them blank when none applies


**Signature Block:**


-


Patient signature with date and time


-


Expiration date (defaults to one year from signature unless an alternative date is specified; an alternative date must be at least 15 days in the future when completing the form)


-


Relationship to patient if signed by a representative


### **Specific Forms for Different Request Types**


Sutter Health provides multiple form options depending on your request:


**Standard Medical Records Authorization:**


-


[English PDF](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-english.pdf)


-


[Spanish PDF](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-spanish.pdf)


-


[Chinese PDF](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-chinese.pdf)


**Radiology Images Authorization (Form SH-0122):**


-


[Separate form required](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/radiology-images-authorization-form.pdf) for X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and ultrasounds on CD


-


Radiology reports come with standard records; actual imaging files need this separate request


## **How to Request Your Sutter Health Medical Records: Online, Phone, and Mail Options**


### **Accessing Records Through Sutter Health's Patient Portal**


Sutter Health's[My Health Online](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/my-health-online) portal gives patients access to records such as after-visit summaries, lab results, medication lists, and imaging reports. Patients can view information available in their account once access is established.


Check whether the portal contains the dates and document types needed, and request additional records when necessary. Certified copies for court still require a formal request through ROI.


### **Direct Phone Contact for Medical Records Department**


**General Sutter Assistance:**


-


**Phone:** 800-478-8837 (800-4SUTTER)


-


Ask to be directed to the appropriate records department and confirm its operating hours


Use phone contact to confirm receipt, check status, and resolve questions. Initial requests should go through written channels (online, fax, or mail).


### **Submitting Requests via Mail or Fax**


Sutter asks requesters to allow up to 15 calendar days after it receives the written request. Confirm any urgent deadline with the records department.


**Fax Submission:**


-


Central ROI Fax:[916-736-5499](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records)


-


Include a fax cover sheet with patient name, DOB, and page count


-


Keep the fax confirmation report for your records


**Mail Submission:**


-


Address: Sutter Health System Office, PO Box 619091, Roseville, CA 95661


-


Use certified mail with return receipt for tracking


-


Include a signed and dated authorization


**Online Submission:**


-


Online request form available on the[Sutter records page](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records)


-


Upload photo ID and supporting documents directly


-


Immediate submission confirmation with reference number

## **Specific Requirements for Requesting a Minor's Medical Records from Sutter Health**


### **Who Can Request a Minor's Records?**


Parents and legal guardians can generally access a minor's records in California, with exceptions:


**Parents and Legal Guardians May Request:**


-


Routine medical care records


-


Emergency treatment documentation


-


Immunization records


-


Hospital admission and discharge summaries


**Restrictions Apply For:**


-


Minors who have consented to their own care for sensitive services. Eligibility to consent independently depends on the service. Some mental-health services have an age-12 threshold and additional conditions; pregnancy-prevention and pregnancy-related care are governed by different provisions


-


Emancipated minors who have legal adult status


-


Cases where a court has limited parental access


### **Necessary Documentation for Minor Requests**


When requesting records for a minor, submit:


-


Completed authorization form signed by a parent or legal guardian


-


Photo ID of the requesting parent or guardian


-


Additional relationship or authority documentation if Sutter requests it


-


Custody order if parents are separated (may be required)


Sutter's instructions exempt parents of minor patients from the additional supporting-document requirement that applies to other representatives. Guardianship, disputed authority, and specially protected care can still require separate consideration, and these situations often benefit from professional retrieval services that understand the documentation requirements.


## **Sutter Health Billing and Medical Records: Understanding the Distinction and Contacting the Right Department**


### **When to Contact Billing vs. Medical Records**


Sutter keeps medical records (clinical documentation) and billing (financial records) in separate departments:


**Medical Records (Release of Information):**


-


Clinic visit notes and provider documentation


-


Hospital admission and discharge summaries


-


Lab and pathology reports


-


Radiology reports and imaging files


-


Surgical and procedure notes


**Billing Department:**


-


Itemized billing statements with CPT codes


-


Insurance claim documentation


-


Payment history and account status


-


Financial assistance applications


### **Direct Phone Numbers for Sutter Health Billing Questions**


For billing inquiries separate from medical records:


-


General routing: Call Sutter's general number at 800-478-8837 and ask to be directed to billing


-


Facility-specific billing contacts are listed on patient statements

## **Template and PDF Options for Your Sutter Health Medical Release Form**


### **Where to Find Official Sutter Health Forms Online**


Official Sutter Health authorization forms are available directly from Sutter's website:


-


[Main Records Request Page](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records) with links to all current forms


-


Forms available in English, Spanish, and Chinese


-


Separate radiology images authorization for imaging files


-


My Health Online enrollment for patient portal access


### **Tips for Completing Your PDF Form Accurately**


Common errors that cause rejections:


-


**Misspelled patient name:** Must match medical records exactly (legal name, not nickname)


-


**Missing photo ID:** Sutter's instructions require identification


-


**Missing sensitive information selections:** Protected categories won't be released without the applicable selections marked


-


**Expiration issues:** Check the authorization's actual expiration; Sutter's form defaults to one year unless an alternative date is specified


-


**Signature issues:** Confirm acceptance of your electronic-signature method with Sutter before submitting


-


**Wrong facility:** Verify where the patient received care


Pre-submission review can identify missing or inconsistent information before a request is sent. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Expect When Requesting Records from Sutter Health**


### **Verifying the Scope of Your Request**


Before submitting, confirm your authorization covers:


-


All Sutter facilities where the patient received care (request "all Sutter Health records" if multiple locations)


-


The complete date range, from the initial injury date through present


-


All record types needed (clinic notes, hospital records, imaging, labs, therapy notes)


-


Only the applicable sensitive-information categories the patient authorizes. The current form also includes abortion-related records, with instructions addressing out-of-state disclosure


### **What to Do if Records Appear Incomplete**


When records arrive, verify completeness by:


-


Checking page count against any index or table of contents


-


Cross-referencing dates of service against billing statements


-


Confirming all requested record types are included


-


Looking for gaps in the treatment timeline


If records look incomplete, contact Sutter's records department right away, referencing your original authorization and what's missing.

## **Understanding HIPAA Compliance: Your Rights When Requesting Sutter Health Medical Records**


### **Your Right to Access Your Medical Information**


Under[HIPAA's Privacy Rule](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/privacy/hipaa-privacy) , patients have the right to:


-


Access and obtain copies of their medical records


-


Request corrections to inaccurate information


-


Receive an accounting of disclosures made by the provider


-


File complaints if access rights are violated


Federal law generally gives providers 30 calendar days to act on patient access requests, while California sets a 15-day timeline for patient copy requests. Evidence Code § 1158 sets a separate five-day availability rule for qualifying pre-litigation attorney requests, covered in the FAQs.


### **Steps to Take if Your Request is Denied**


If Sutter Health denies a record request, you have options:


-


Request a written explanation for the denial


-


Submit an appeal through the Privacy Office at 855-771-4220


-


File a HIPAA complaint with the Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights


-


For litigation purposes, pursue records through formal discovery


The Privacy Office can be reached at: Privacy Office, Office of Legal and Risk Services, 2200 River Plaza Dr., Sacramento, CA 95833.


## **Efficiently Obtaining Old Medical Records from Sutter Health: Best Practices**


### **Understanding Sutter Health's Record Retention Policies**


California physicians generally must retain records for at least seven years after the last service. General acute-care hospitals generally must preserve records for at least seven years after discharge. Hospital records for unemancipated minors must be retained until at least age 19 and never for less than seven years. Longer requirements may apply.


Older records may require an archive search. Ask Sutter to confirm availability and expected completion; off-site storage doesn't automatically extend an applicable legal deadline.


### **Strategies for Locating Records from Previous Years**


For historical records:


-


Provide as much identifying information as possible (previous addresses, old phone numbers, maiden names)


-


Include medical record numbers from old paperwork if available


-


Specify approximate treatment dates even if exact dates are unknown


-


Request "all available records" rather than limiting to specific dates if unsure of treatment history


### **What Information to Provide for Older Records**


Include:


-


Patient's name at time of treatment (including maiden name if applicable)


-


Address at time of treatment


-


All possible date ranges


-


Specific facility names if known


-


Any available reference numbers from old records or billing statements

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it take to get medical records from Sutter Health?**


Sutter asks requesters to allow up to 15 calendar days after it receives the written request, consistent with California Health & Safety Code § 123110. For qualifying requests under California Evidence Code § 1158, records must be made available for inspection and copying within five days after presentation of the written authorization; this applies before an action is filed or a defendant appears, and it means availability, not necessarily delivery. Confirm any urgent deadline with the records department. Codes Health describes typical retrieval in a couple of weeks, though Sutter-specific turnaround varies.


### **Is there a fee for requesting medical records from Sutter Health?**


Usually, yes. California law permits specified copying charges, but HIPAA patient-access requests are also subject to reasonable, cost-based fee limits. A state per-page allowance doesn't automatically establish the permissible charge, and qualifying public-benefit requests may be free. For attorney requests[under § 1158](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EVID&sectionNum=1158) , the fee structure is $0.10 per page for standard copies, $0.20 per page for microfilm, clerical costs up to $16 per hour, plus postage. When records are made available for inspection or photocopying at the custodian's business under § 1158(f), the compliance fee is capped at $15, plus qualifying third-party off-site retrieval and return costs. Sutter provides fee estimates before processing.


### **Can I request medical records for a family member from Sutter Health?**


A patient can authorize Sutter to send records to a family member. A person signing or exercising access rights as the patient's legal representative must establish the relevant authority, such as a power of attorney that allows records release, guardianship or conservatorship papers, or executor documentation for deceased patients. Sutter requires identification and supporting authority documents for representative requests, but its instructions expressly exempt parents of minor patients from the additional supporting-document requirement. Minors who consented to their own care under California law may limit parental access.


### **What if I need to amend information in my Sutter Health medical records?**


Under HIPAA, patients can request amendments by writing to Sutter's Privacy Office, explaining what's incorrect and why. The provider has 60 days to respond and may deny requests in certain circumstances, such as when the information is accurate. If denied, you can submit a statement of disagreement to be included in your record.


### **Does Sutter Health provide records electronically?**


Yes. The online request system on Sutter's[records request page](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records) lets you request electronic delivery, and you can specify preferences on the authorization form. Options include encrypted email, unencrypted email (not recommended for sensitive records), encrypted CD or USB, portal delivery, and fax with a 50-page limit. The My Health Online portal also lets patients view information available in their account, including lab results, after-visit summaries, and medication histories.


### **Where can I find the official Sutter Health medical records request form?**


Official forms are on Sutter's[records request page](https://www.sutterhealth.org/patient-resources/records-planning/request-medical-records) . The primary form is the "Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Health Information" (Form SH-0009), available in[English](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-english.pdf) ,[Spanish](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-spanish.pdf) , and[Chinese](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/medical-authorization-release-form-chinese.pdf) . A separate[radiology images authorization form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/sutterhealt962c-sutterhealt8fce-production57cc-4860/media/Project/SutterHealth/SutterHealth/Files/PatientResources/records-planning/radiology-images-authorization-form.pdf) (SH-0122) is required for X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and other imaging files on CD.
